children: Velo3D’s third-quarter revenue rose 49.9% year over year, while its net loss widened. Higher printer-system sales, average selling prices and product mix, along with increased RPS production, lifted revenue; gross margin improved with favorable mix, inventory-reserve adjustments and manufacturing efficiencies, but operating expenses increased.
¹ Reported as “Total Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Basic and Diluted”.
: Third-quarter bookings were $29M, versus $18M a year earlier; backlog was $40M, versus $21M.
: 3D printer and parts revenue increased 57.0% to $18.8M, driven by more systems sold, higher average selling prices and product mix, and higher RPS production.
: Gross margin rose to 26.5% from 3.2%, reflecting favorable product mix, inventory-reserve adjustments and improved manufacturing efficiencies.
: The approximately 289,000-square-foot Livermore facility commenced its lease July 1 and is expected to expand RPS capabilities and manufacturing capacity; it is not yet operating at scale.
: 2026 capital expenditures are expected at $10M to $20M, down from the prior $40M to $50M range, primarily due to shifting planned spending into 2027.
